title: Stale SCHC expiry abort can terminate a newer T=0 transfer
description: _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager keeps the pending-expiry control for a key after an expired context's tombstone matures into a floor. If the caller does not drain expire_due() before a newer-counter opener arrives (possible through the public LinkLayer APIs after a paused maintenance loop), receive() admits the replacement transfer but leaves the old Receiver-Abort queued. A later expire_authenticated_schc_reassembly() then emits that stale abort for the same peer/Rule ID, and because T=0 has no session discriminator it can abort the new transfer. When newer authenticated state supersedes the floor, atomically retire any pending control for the old state (or require/drain it before admission), and add a clock-driven regression covering expiry -> undrained control -> newer opener -> drain.
